proposals.relationship: McPherson credits Woodward’s example of combining new historical interpretation with prose for a broad audience as shaping his approach to writing.
proposals.evidence_note: His own NEH answer specifies Tom Watson, Origins of the New South and Strange Career of Jim Crow and Woodward’s criticism of his writing. Lindley answer explicitly identifies a formative influence on writing. Distinct kind from existing edge_1799 commissioning contribution; no claim that every interpretation derives from Woodward, or new reading of the named books or draft materials.
primary_locators: Lindley question beginning Your books, including Battle Cry, are praised, answer beginning I believe that a historian has a duty; NEH Interview, question Vann Woodward ... What did he teach you about writing history? and full answer.

proposals.relationship: McPherson names Hofstadter as a formative model for historical writing that reaches academic and interested lay audiences.
proposals.evidence_note: Own recollection explicitly joins Hofstadter with Allan Nevins and Arthur Schlesinger Jr.; all retain credit. This is a writing/audience influence during graduate school and after, not evidence that McPherson adopted consensus historiography or a specified Hofstadter book. No original reading of those authors in this dossier.
primary_locators: Lindley writing-influences question and answer, final sentences naming Woodward, Nevins, Schlesinger Jr. and Hofstadter.

proposals.relationship: McPherson uses Foner’s account of fugitive slaves and interracial aid networks to explain how a numerically small movement intensified sectional conflict.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2015 review endorses the political force of escapees and publicizes Foner’s New York evidence. Madeline Lewis’s discovery of Gay’s Record of Fugitives, Gay and Louis Napoleon’s work and enslaved people’s initiative retain credit. Specific resource in this essay, not a claim that Foner originated McPherson’s broader emancipation interpretation. Full Gateway to Freedom and record independently unread.
primary_locators: Paragraph beginning No one knows how many slaves escaped through the next paragraph Southern demands; paragraphs beginning Foner is one of our foremost historians and Gay’s Record of Fugitives enables Foner; final paragraph beginning After chronicling these events.

proposals.relationship: McPherson draws on Faust’s account of the Good Death and the wartime/postwar identification and reburial of soldiers to connect mourning with new national obligations.
proposals.evidence_note: Specific argumentative use in own 2008 review coexists with his reservations about theology and weighting costs against achievements. Mark Schantz supplies a distinct complementary account of the culture of death; Faust is not credited with his claims. Original This Republic of Suffering unread. The reverse-direction criticism key is already reserved by Faust’s queued dossier and is not duplicated.
